summary: The compact gabled form, brown body, pale roof, single southeast entrance, and northeast-side window make the studio broadly recognizable. However, prominent material and entrance details need correction before it is ready.

orientation.summary: SV1 is geolocated northwest/northeast of the cabin and looks west, obliquely exposing the southeast (-u) gable and northeast (+v) side. Its white glazed door is on the screen-left southeast gable, while the tall window is on the northeast side. The labeled face sheet and actual inventory correspond: one principal door on -u (129° SE), a window on +v (39° NE), and no duplicated principal portal.

issues.problem: The principal southeast door is rendered as a plain solid slab, losing the conspicuous glazed multi-pane upper section visible in SV1.
issues.fix: Replace it with a white glazed door featuring a clearly readable multi-pane window and retain the small two-step stoop.

issues.problem: The wall finish reads as regular red brick, whereas the reference cabin has warm brown shingle or overlapping-board siding.
issues.fix: Use simplified horizontal shingle courses in a muted reddish brown, with enough relief or linework to remain legible at miniature scale.

issues.problem: The pale roof reads as tiled shingles rather than the smooth light metal roof characteristic of the reference.
issues.fix: Simplify the roof surface and add restrained standing seams while preserving the bright projecting white edges.
